sections.title: Form and habitat
sections.text: Nepenthes inermis is a climbing or epiphytic carnivorous plant endemic to the western Sumatran highlands, at about 1,500–2,590 m. It grows in mossy forest or summit vegetation.

sections.title: Leaves and pitchers
sections.text: The leaves bear a tendril ending in a pitcher trap. The upper pitchers are about 5.5–9 cm long, narrow below and funnel-shaped above; their peristome is almost absent. A pitcher is a modified leaf, not a flower or fruit.

sections.title: Inflorescence
sections.text: The small unisexual flowers are borne separately in racemes. The fruit is a dry capsule that splits into valves and releases seeds.
